title: Expose fail-closed tenant capability eligibility and governed remediation

phases.objective: Project the canonical Platform Plugin resolver decision into a tenant-safe eligibility state with typed blockers and bounded managed-repair dry-run guidance, without claiming dispatch or repair authority when credential, resource-authority, approval, or security gates fail.

e2e_journeys.actor: Authenticated tenant user resolving a Platform Plugin capability
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: POST /tenant/platform/plugins/resolve after canonical User-JWT and active-membership authorization
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The response exposes ready, blocked, approval_required, unavailable, or deprecated eligibility plus typed repair classes. Missing runtime binding or smoke certification may expose a bounded managed-repair dry-run plan, while actual execution remains exclusively behind tenant-managed-execution-v1 authority, approval, idempotency and readback.
steps: Resolve the requested capability through the existing canonical Platform Plugin resolver and its fail-closed security gates.
Strip the admin-only decision trace projection from the tenant response as before.
Project required denied or unevaluated gates into tenant-safe blocker codes and repair classes without reading secrets or executing a repair.
Return ready only when the canonical resolver reports execution.will_execute=true.
For an exact canonical plugin+selector identity, map only missing runtime binding and missing/expired smoke certification to managed_repair_available.
Build a deterministic dry-run managed-execution request template using a dedicated repair capability, exact hashed plugin-operation resource identity and stable idempotency key.
Require parent ticket linkage, managed_handoff approval and managed_operator role; do not authorize Apply from discovery.
Keep target authority, credential, approval, skill and canonical-policy blockers outside managed repair so the repair surface cannot grant itself authority or credentials.
Route any later repair execution through /managed-execution-runs, where canonical User-JWT scope binding and #4449 authority/resource-grant revalidation apply before state mutation.
Require post-repair readback through /tenant/platform/plugins/resolve and disallow automatic retry after unknown outcome.
assertions: A dispatch-ready canonical resolver decision projects to status=ready with zero blockers.
Missing action/tool binding with canonical plugin+selector identity projects to blocked + managed_repair_available and produces only a dry-run plan.
Missing/expired smoke certification with canonical plugin+selector identity projects to blocked + managed_repair_available and produces only a dry-run plan.
If canonical plugin+selector identity is unavailable, those blockers remain platform_admin_required fail-closed.
Missing credential projects to blocked + user_action_required with credential/OAuth intake guidance only.
Multiple eligible connection ambiguity projects to blocked + tenant_admin_action_available and never selects a first candidate.
Target resource authority remains platform_admin_required and is never auto-granted by managed repair.
The dry-run request template does not accept tenant_id or user_id from discovery; canonical route authorization owns those principal fields.
The managed repair capability requires managed_operation, managed_handoff approval, stable idempotency and readback; discovery sets apply_authorized_by_projection=false.
Migration 1052 registers metadata/readiness only and performs no repair, provider call, resource-grant creation, credential read, Production mutation, or external write.
A pending governed approval projects to approval_required rather than ready.
Disabled and deprecated plugin states project to unavailable and deprecated respectively.
